title: GROUP BY (SQL) | InterSystems SQL Reference | InterSystems IRIS Data Platform 2026.1

examples.sql: SELECT Home_State,COUNT(Home_State) FROM Sample.Person GROUP BY Home_State
SELECT DISTINCT BY(Home_State) Home_State,COUNT(Home_State) FROM Sample.Person
SELECT Home_State,(SELECT COUNT(Home_State) FROM Sample.Person) FROM Sample.Person GROUP BY Home_State
SELECT DISTINCT * FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS mynum FROM Sample.Person GROUP BY Home_State) AS Sub ORDER BY Sub.mynum
SELECT AVG(Age) FROM Sample.Person WHERE Name %STARTSWITH 'ZZZZ'

SELECT Home_City FROM Sample.Person GROUP BY Home_City /* groups together Home_City values by their uppercase letter values returns the name of each grouped city in uppercase letters. Thus, 'NEW YORK' is returned. */

SELECT %EXACT(Home_City) FROM Sample.Person GROUP BY Home_City /* groups together Home_City values by their uppercase letter values returns the name of a grouped city in original letter case. Thus, 'New York' or 'new york' may be returned, but not both. */

SELECT Home_City FROM Sample.Person GROUP BY %EXACT(Home_City) /* groups together Home_City values by their original letter case returns the name of each grouped city in original letter case. Thus, both 'New York' and 'new york' are returned as separate groups. */
SELECT Name AS Initial,COUNT(Name) AS SameInitial,%EXACT(Name) AS Example FROM Sample.Person GROUP BY %SQLUPPER(Name,2)
